reason: The stem cell has a membrane-growth slot, and phospholipids supply membrane material.
expectation: The phospholipids will fill the membrane-growth slot.

effect: The phospholipids filled the membrane-growth slot; the cell still needs cytoplasm growth and DNA replication.
reason: New cell proteins are the evident material for the cytoplasm-growth slot.
expectation: The proteins will fill the cytoplasm-growth slot.

effect: The proteins filled the cytoplasm-growth slot, leaving DNA replication to prepare.
reason: DNA-building nucleotides are the evident material for the remaining replication slot.
expectation: The nucleotides will fill the DNA-replication slot and prepare the cell to copy its genome.

effect: The cell has grown and copied its DNA; the new goal is to separate two living daughter cells.
reaction: The distinction between doubled DNA and still-joined chromosome copies is useful.
reason: The mitotic spindle is depicted attaching to paired chromosomes, making it the likely next step in separating their copies.
expectation: The spindle will help separate the copied chromosome sets.

effect: The spindle separated the chromosome sets, but the cytoplasm remains continuous.
reaction: The distinction between chromosome separation and cell division is clear.
reason: The contractile ring is depicted narrowing the cell at its equator, where the remaining division must occur.
expectation: The ring will constrict the cell and separate it into two daughter cells.

effect: The contractile ring separated the cell into two complete living descendants, completing the goal.
reaction: The final distinction between dividing living cells and assembling parts was clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Separating the chromosome sets before dividing the cytoplasm was worthwhile: the successive picture descriptions made those distinct events clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: The first two slot fittings were predictable and repetitive, although they made the material needed for growth explicit.

surprise.text: The replication inset usefully clarified that DNA amount doubles while the sister chromosome copies remain joined until separation.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless; the named slots and picture descriptions made the choices clear. The term “sister chromatids,” however, was not explicitly defined beyond the inset showing joined copies.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the chromosome-separation and division sequence made me curious how the descendants would contribute to later anatomical structures.
